text:
maria_sales: FYI — Varela POC inbound. Customer wants to run a custom variant 'varela-13b-cust' in Dedicated. They asked for: compatibility check, latency pricing, KMS + VPC details. Can we triage?

ajay_se: Got it. Do we have the model artifact + tokenizer and an expected workload profile?

maria_sales: Sending specifics: model tar on their S3, tokenizer is a custom BPE (not vanilla llama). Workload: peak ~100 rps, steady 30 rps; avg prompt ~450 tokens + 150 response tokens; p95 latency target ~200ms. KV-caching desired. Customer is healthcare (will sign BAA). Need private/VPC.

ajay_se: Thanks. A couple quick checks from my side:
- Is the tokenizer deterministic? custom tokenizers sometimes explode token counts.
- Any special ops (rotary variants / rmsnorm forks)?
- Are they expecting 8-bit quant (q4_0/q8_0) or FP16?

maria_sales: They said q4_0 for cost reasons. Model is a minor fork of Llama-style arch with an RMSNorm tweak. Tokenizer -> custom-tokenizer-v2, determinism unknown but they claim identical outputs to reference.

ajay_se: Ok. Two action items I can run: (1) quick compatibility scan, (2) perf profile on Dedicated config. Need model artifact + tokenizer files and a sample corpus. Can you get them to upload to a signed S3?

maria_sales: I asked them to share a presigned link — should arrive today. ETA from customer: EOD. Also asked for SOC2 + privacy contact.

redwood-deploy-bot: model-scan queued: tools/model-scan --model s3://varela/pubs/v1.tar.gz --tokenizer s3://varela/tokenizer/v2.zip --profile quick-compat

lucy_eng: Quick notes from infra side: For q4_0 + KV cache + 200ms p95 at 100rps, plan is Dedicated single node with 2 x L40x (nvlink) and autoscale headroom. If tokenizer expands token count by 20-30% we'd need to re-evaluate memory. Realistic timeline to validate: 48-72h for scan + quant perf pass.

ajay_se: Lucy, can we run an isolated perf job with the customer's sample corpus? I can prep the test harness. Also need to ensure tokenization runs in native C++ binary or our Python path — sometimes custom tokenizer slows pipeline.

lucy_eng: Yes. Send the corpus + tokenizer binary. If it's python-only, recommend we containerize the tokenizer and run it on the same node as the model runner to avoid network overhead.

maria_sales: I'll collect artifacts. Also customer asked about pricing for a short reserved window (1 month) vs on-demand Dedicated bursts — they want an estimate today to include in a procurement doc.

tina_prod: Ballpark pricing: short-reserve for the node config above ~ $3,200/month for a single Dedicated node with priority capacity. On-demand bursts roughly 1.6x that hourly. That's rough; exact quote needs procurement. Also note there will be token unit costs for Hosted if they opt fallback.

kevin_security: Security/questions from my side:
- We need to confirm data residency (which region), KMS/HSM requirements, and logging retention.
- Need to see the model's training data provenance (PHI concerns).
- We require SOC2/ISO27001 + vendor contacts for legal.

maria_sales: They confirmed region=us-west-2, will use customer-managed KMS (HSM), and will share training provenance docs — they said it's de-identified but we're awaiting evidence.

ajay_se: Technical blocker: RMSNorm variant may change weights layout. I recommend we run our adapter script to normalize the layer norm weights and reserialize into Redwood-compatible format. Sample adapter command:```bash
python tools/adapter.py --input /tmp/varela/v1.pt --norm rmsnorm --out /tmp/varela/normalized.pt
```

lucy_eng: Also run the compatibility check tool once normalized:```bash
tools/model-scan --model /tmp/varela/normalized.pt --tokenizer /tmp/varela/tokenizer.zip --output /tmp/reports/varela-compat.json
```Expect the scan to flag kernel-ops that need stubs; we can patch or fall back to less-optimized kernels.

ajay_se: Timeline check: If artifacts arrive today, I can run adapter + scan in ~24h; Lucy and infra can do perf profile in the next 24–48h. So overall ~3 business days for a go/no-go and a perf report.

maria_sales: Great. I'll push for artifacts now.

kevin_security: Also: for healthcare PII/PHI we need audit log retention 1 year and optional data egress limits. If they insist on air-gapped on-prem, that changes pricing/ops — call that out.

tina_prod: Noted. If they sign Private deployment + BAA + HSM, our onboarding checklist: catalog entry, variant metadata, perf profile, quant profile, security sign-off, rollout plan. I'll prepare a draft checklist and a preliminary cost estimate to share with procurement.

maria_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll post the presigned links when I have them. Can folks @mention if blocked?

ajay_se: @lucy_eng please ping me when perf cluster is provisioned.

lucy_eng: Will do.

redwood-deploy-bot: model-scan started: job-id rdb-scan-7591

maria_sales: Received presigned link from customer (sharing in DM).

ajay_se: Awesome — starting adapter + scan now. I'll drop the report once done. :thumbsup:

redwood-deploy-bot: model-scan complete: job-id rdb-scan-7591; result: compatibility-issues=2; report: /tmp/reports/varela-compat.json

ajay_se: Scan found two minor ops mismatches (custom rmsnorm layout + rotary multiplier op). Both are patchable — estimated dev time 1 day to add an adapter and optimized kernel fallback. Also tokenizer expands tokens ~12% on our sample, so memory headroom is fine for 2xL40x.

lucy_eng: Perf pass queued. If perf looks good we can spin a short reserved node and give them a stress-run.

maria_sales: Perfect. I'll update the customer: ETA for go/no-go = 3 business days, provisional pricing + checklist to follow.

kevin_security: I'll start prep on the security checklist and send the fields we need for the questionnaire.

maria_sales: Thanks all.
